headline: High risk of shared-filesystem prompt injection and cascading errors; both agents can write/read the same workspace and execute tools by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write filesystem content, and both expose MCP/tool use. Goose shares state via filesystem and Windsurf shares via local filesystem plus clipboard, so attacker-controlled files or copied content can bridge them. Because Windsurf can ingest clipboard and Goose treats files as workspace inputs, prompt injection is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF either agent reads content from a shared workspace file created by the other agent, injection is possible.
IF the operator copies one agent's output into the other's prompt or clipboard, the bridge becomes active.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable clipboard-based handoff for Windsurf.
Require human review of any file both agents may read.
Use a read-only export format for inter-agent transfer.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging or content signing between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: The pair shares filesystem-based state and both touch source code/files in the working directory, so data written by one can be read by the other. Goose also has broad network egress and handles model provider keys and extension tokens, while Windsurf can access workspace files and clipboard. This creates a realistic leakage path for sensitive local files, though not enough evidence for a higher severity.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared workspace, the other agent can read them.
IF Goose forwards secrets or file contents to configured model providers, those contents can leave the machine.
mitigations: Keep secrets outside the shared workspace.
Use separate OS users or containers.
Redact credentials before either agent reads files.
Disable network egress for tasks involving secrets.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, package installation, and git-state modification, and both share state via filesystem. In default use, concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt git state without locking. The overlap is broad and the blast radius includes repository damage and lost work.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout, conflicting writes can occur.
IF either agent auto-applies edits while the other is active, race conditions become likely.
mitigations: Run only one agent per checkout.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use git worktrees for parallel tasks.
Commit or stash after each agent step.
requires-engineering: add file-level locking or orchestrator coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Both agents can act on files and git state, and Windsurf’s Cascade loop plus Goose’s tool use can turn one agent’s output into the other’s next action without a verification barrier. That makes mistaken code, commands, or file edits propagate across the pair in default workflows, with potentially irreversible repository changes.
conditions: IF one agent's generated patch is pasted or synced into the other's workspace, the second may act on it as authoritative.
IF auto-execute is enabled in Windsurf, erroneous instructions can become immediate actions.
mitigations: Require diff review before applying either agent's output.
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf.
Use a checklist for commands generated by Goose.
Limit each agent to read-only analysis until approval.
requires-engineering: insert a verification gate between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are closed-source/open-source mixed? Goose is open-source while Windsurf is closed-source, and both handle source code and files in the cwd/workspace. The profiles do not document residency or retention guarantees, so compliance mismatch is uncertain; per rubric, uncertainty should not be downgraded. The main issue is potential policy mismatch on code and file handling rather than a proven residency breach.
conditions: IF the workspace contains regulated data, both agents may process it under undocumented retention policies.
IF organizational policy requires documented residency or deletion guarantees, the pair may fail compliance review.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Review vendor retention and residency docs before use.
Use synthetic or masked data for agentic tasks.
Restrict both agents to non-regulated repositories.
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA and formal compliance attestation.
